paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Jesus gives us two parables, and they land in the same place: how we come to God. The first one, He tells about our need to pray "at all times and not lose heart" (Luke 18:1). A widow keeps showing up to a judge who "neither feared God nor respected men," and her asking wears him down (Luke 18:2, 5). Jesus says, "Listen to the words of the unjust judge," and then asks, "Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night?" (Luke 18:6-7).

Now hear this, because it's the good news. That judge had to be worn down. God doesn't. Jesus says He "will promptly carry out justice on their behalf" (Luke 18:8). So when the answer feels slow and you're tempted to quit, keep praying. You're not bothering a grumpy judge. You're talking to a God who hears you.

The second parable is about HOW we pray. Jesus tells it to some who "trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt" (Luke 18:9). One man read God his résumé. The other said, "God, have mercy on me, a sinner!" and Jesus says that man "went home justified" (Luke 18:13-14). So come to God as you are, with no list and no pointing at the guy next to you. "The one who humbles himself will be exalted" (Luke 18:14), and I say that as a stamper who once spent years in the back of a junk drawer.
